result.title: CogArena: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents on Interactive Behavioral Experiments
result.comment: 28 pages, 4 figures, 11 tables. Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track). Code: https://github.com/kiante-fernandez/CogArena. Leaderboard: https://cog-arena.vercel.app
result.summary: Claims about the cognitive capabilities of large language models are typically tested by translating behavioral paradigms into text prompts, bypassing the visual interfaces and time pressure through which human participants actually engage with experiments. At the same time, AI agents can now complete online behavioral tasks and produce human-like data, which raises concerns that online datasets in the social and behavioral sciences are increasingly open to contamination. We introduce CogArena, a benchmark of ten experimental paradigms from the social and behavioral sciences. Agents complete the experiments through a standard web browser, working with the same visual stimuli and response interfaces that online participants use. A three-level scoring procedure evaluates whether the agent completed the task, how accurately it performed, and whether its data show the behavioral signatures each paradigm reliably produces in people. Across four multimodal models, each run ten times per task, we find that finishing an experiment and reproducing its signatures are different things. Many sessions did not finish, and those that did reproduced some signatures reliably and others not at all. CogArena provides the tasks, scoring code, and a public leaderboard for new submissions.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 CogArena，将社会与行为科学的十个实验范式搬到标准浏览器中，让多模态智能体面对与人类被试相同的视觉刺激和作答界面，并用「完成—准确—行为签名」三级评分考察四个模型各十次运行的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其三级评分区分「完成任务」与「复现范式稳定行为签名」，可能为核查 LVR 中答案正确但 latent 推理未真正使用视觉证据这类结果与过程脱节问题提供评价思路，但任务本身不涉及内部状态或推理机制，联系较远。
